headline: Ex-Air Force chief Sheikh Abdul Hannan arrested in Qatar over corruption
summary: The former Air Vice Marshal is accused of laundering money abroad and acquiring assets worth crores of taka beyond his known sources of income.
details: Former Bangladesh Air Force chief Air Vice Marshal (retd) Sheikh Abdul Hannan has been arrested in Qatar on October 15, according to the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).
The ACC filed a case against Hannan on July 27, 2025, alleging he acquired assets beyond his known sources of income and engaged in suspicious financial transactions.
Investigations found evidence of assets worth Tk 3.28 crore acquired beyond his known sources, along with suspicious transactions involving more than Tk 14.08 crore.
The commission's inquiry, which began in February 2025, also investigated allegations of abuse of power, bribery, recruitment irregularities, and embezzlement.
The case was filed under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, and the Prevention of Corruption Act.
As part of the probe, the ACC sought information on Hannan's assets in Qatar, Canada, and other countries through the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit.
A court order has been obtained to attach and freeze the movable and immovable assets of both Hannan and his wife.
caption:
A former Air Force chief has been arrested in Qatar. He is accused of laundering millions and acquiring illegal assets.

Former Bangladesh Air Force chief Air Vice Marshal (retd) Sheikh Abdul Hannan has been arrested in Qatar on October 15, according to the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).

The ACC filed a case against Hannan on July 27, 2025, alleging he acquired assets beyond his known sources of income and engaged in suspicious financial transactions.

Investigations found evidence of assets worth Tk 3.28 crore acquired beyond his known sources, along with suspicious transactions involving more than Tk 14.08 crore.

The commission's inquiry, which began in February 2025, also investigated allegations of abuse of power, bribery, recruitment irregularities, and embezzlement.

The case was filed under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, and the Prevention of Corruption Act.

As part of the probe, the ACC sought information on Hannan's assets in Qatar, Canada, and other countries through the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit.

A court order has been obtained to attach and freeze the movable and immovable assets of both Hannan and his wife.
